items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO HIGHER EDUCATION

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to establishing the "help individuals reach employment program" (HIRE)
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2603

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
establishing the "help individuals reach employment program" (HIRE)

 PURPOSE :

To establish the Help Individuals Reach Employment Program (HIRE).

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

This bill provides for the creation of the "Help Individuals Reach
Employment Program (HIRE).

To participate in HIRE an applicant must have : 1) received an
undergraduate degree from the State University of New York (SUNY) or
City University of New York (CUNY) and have achieved a GPA of 3.0 or
higher; 2) completed their degree in no more than 5 years or 6 years
if the degree typically requires 5 years to complete; 3) completed an
approved experiential learning activity as defined by the board of
trustees; 4) graduated and sought employment for at least 6 months
prior to the date of application; 5) been unsuccessful in obtaining
full time employment; 6) provided documentation that such applicant
has sought employment for such a job in New York State; and 7) applied
for the degree enhancement for employment program within one year
after the date of graduation.

The SUNY and CUNY trustees must establish or identify existing
certificate programs that provide skills for college graduates to
enhance their employment marketability and these certificate programs
shall be made free of charge to the applicant. The SUNY and CUNY
trustees will also work with the Department of Labor to identify what
the job market and industry needs are. If SUNY or CUNY does not offer
certificate programs that meet the requirements of this section or if
the current programs are at capacity or cannot be expanded to admit
all eligible applicants, those programs can be offered in an online
format.

This measure also allows an applicant to take a certificate program at
the campus where they graduated, if available. If not, the applicant
can take the certificate program at a community college free of
charge.

Each SUNY and CUNY institution that confers 4 year degrees must inform
all incoming freshmen and transfer students about anticipated job
availability per major, approximate salary ranges, which degrees
typically require a graduate degree or additional education and about
the institution's undergraduate student employment rates within one
year of such students' graduation.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Higher education is extremely important in the current job market.
However, making sure students are aware of outcomes per degree is also
just as vital. This bill would create the "HIRE" program to help
ensure employment outcomes for students graduating from a SUNY or CUNY
institution and provide them with tools necessary to find employment
after school by providing an opportunity for additional training for
enhanced marketability for a job if an applicant to the HIRE program
has had trouble finding employment.

It is important to foster better employment outcomes after investing
so much time, money and effort in higher education.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016 S.7646.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect one year after it shall have become a law.
